harvest: Harvest the flowering tops at the start of flowering and shortly after the leaves appear
preservation: Dry quickly in a well-ventilated, dry place, away from direct sunlight, and store in sealed containers away from light, dust and moisture. Replace your stock annually.

harvest: Harvest throughout the summer, from May to September
preservation: Dry in the shade in a well-ventilated place and store in containers away from moisture

harvest: Harvest during the flowering season, from June to September
preservation: Hang them in bunches to dry in the shade and store them in a cool, dry place

harvest: Harvest the flowers before they are fully open, preferably in the morning
preservation: Dry in a dry, well-ventilated place, taking care not to expose the flower heads to direct sunlight, and store in wooden or cardboard boxes

harvest: Harvest the flowers (female inflorescences) from summer through to autumn
preservation: Dry in the shade and store in airtight containers

harvest: The flowering tops are harvested from May to August, and the leaves from April to July
preservation: Dry the parts in the shade and store them in containers away from light and moisture

harvest: Harvest the flowers at the start of flowering or during flowering; harvest the roots and fruits from autumn to spring
preservation: Dry the flowers in the shade and store them in sealed containers. Dry the roots in the sun and store them in glass jars. Dry the fruits, crush them and sieve them, taking care to store them in glass jars

harvest: Harvest the leaves in late spring. Harvest the roots and seeds in early autumn
preservation: Dry the roots and leaves in the shade, taking care to store them separately: use airtight containers for the roots and canvas or paper bags for the leaves. Then dry the seeds by placing them in direct sunlight. Keep all parts in a dry place

harvest: Harvest the flowers just before they are fully open; harvest the leaves whilst they are in bloom
preservation: Dry in the shade immediately after harvesting and store in sealed containers, protected from air and moisture

harvest: Harvest the roots in autumn, and the leaves and flowers before they bloom
preservation: Cut the root lengthways and dry it in the sun. Leave the leaves and flowers to dry in the shade and store them in plastic bags

harvest: Harvest the roots in autumn, taking care to discard any that have become woody. The leaves should be harvested in summer, before flowering, and the fruits should be picked before they ripen
preservation: The roots can be sun-dried and stored in dust-proof bags, whilst the leaves and seeds, which have been dried in the shade and in the open air, can be stored in wooden or cardboard containers

harvest: The falling of the seeds from the central umbel, which is the first to flower and whose fruits are the most fragrant, determines the harvest date
preservation: The seeds should be dried in the shade or in the sun, and then shelled. It is recommended to store them in containers in a dry place

preservation: Harvest the leaves during the summer, before the plants come into full bloom

harvest: Harvest at any time of year
preservation: Harvest at any time of year

harvest: Collect the branches in spring and the buds in winter
preservation: Dry the branches in the shade and store them in paper or cloth bags. Dry the buds in the sun and store them in tightly sealed containers

harvest: Harvest the petals and the seedpods, emptied of their seeds, during flowering
preservation: Dry in the shade and store in containers away from light, moisture and air

harvest: Harvest the stigmas of the flowers at the start of flowering
preservation: Dry in the sun and store in canvas bags away from light and moisture

harvest: Harvest before the flowers have fully opened, preferably in the morning
preservation: Dry immediately after harvesting in a dry, well-ventilated place, taking care to separate the flowers from their calyxes beforehand

vernacular_name: St John’s wort (EN); Erba di San Giovanni (IT);

harvest: The leaves can be harvested in late summer. The husk, when the fruit is harvested
preservation: Dry the leaves in the shade and store them in paper or wooden containers. The husks should be sun-dried and stored away from moisture and dust

harvest: Pick the flower heads early in the morning when the sun is out, during the summer
preservation: Dry in bunches hung up, away from light, and store in airtight containers

harvest: Harvest at the start of flowering (spring–summer)
preservation: Dry in a cool, well-ventilated and dry place, tied in bunches, and store in paper bags to protect them from moisture

harvest: Harvest during the summer, once the plant has finished flowering
preservation: Dry in the shade and in the open air, and store in airtight containers

harvest: Uproot the rhizome at any time of year, except in winter
preservation: Clean the rhizomes, dry them in the sun and store them in wooden containers, protected from woodworm and air. Replace them frequently as they spoil easily

harvest: Harvest just before flowering
preservation: Dry in the shade and store in paper or cloth bags

harvest: The roots should be harvested at the end of summer. The aerial parts are harvested from spring to autumn
preservation: Dry the plant in the shade and store it in boxes or crates, protected from damp and dust. The roots should be dried in the sun and stored in canvas bags
